prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has largely completed and passed the first and second-year courses of the degree. This is because this subject generally requires a solid understanding of basic fundamentals that will facilitate the understanding and application of more advanced concepts studied in this subject.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering whose purpose is the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in competence G01.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Ability to adapt to new situations.
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability for autonomous and deep learning.
Ability to interpret technical documentation.
Ability for critical reasoning.
Ability for autonomous learning.
Competence in the critical contextualization of knowledge, establishing interrelationships with social, economic, and environmental issues, local and/or global.
Competence in the application of ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional behaviors.
Understand and analyze Industrial Quality Management, and have resources for the design and implementation of Quality Systems.

syllabus_topics: Block 1: Fundamentals, Advanced Tools, and Lean Manufacturing
Chapter 1. Quality management: History, concept, and competitive advantage.
Chapter 2. The philosophy of quality gurus: Deming, Juran, Ishikawa, Crosby, etc.
Chapter 3. Quality Assurance (Lean Manufacturing): Toyota System, Poka-Yoke, Zero Defects.
Chapter 4. Problem-solving tools: The 7 classic tools and the 7 new management tools.
Chapter 5. Quality Engineering: Taguchi Method and Robust Design.
Block 2. Statistical Quality Control
Chapter 6. Quality Control by attributes. Quality Control by variables.
6.1. The Statistical Method.
6.2. Statistical Distributions of Interest.
6.3. Statistics and Quality. Process in a state of control. Tolerance limits.
6.4. Capability measures. 6-sigma Processes.
6.5. Calculation of capability measures with Statgraphics.
6.6. Control by attributes. Control Charts.
6.7. Control by variables. Control Charts.
6.8. Control Charts with Statgraphics.
6.9. Acceptance control. Sampling plans.
6.10. Acceptance control with Statgraphics.
Block 3: Total Quality Management, Techniques, and Services
Chapter 7. The Total Quality Management (TQM) model: Customer orientation, processes, and leadership.
Chapter 8. Operational quality management techniques: QFD (Quality Function Deployment), FMEA (Failure Mode and Effects Analysis), Quality Circles, Benchmarking, and 5S.
Chapter 9. Quality management in services: Concepts, characteristics, and measurement models (SERVQUAL).
Chapter 10. Introduction to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Industry: Concept of sustainable development and its importance in engineering.
teaching_methods: Lectures (expository, explanatory, and demonstrative presentations, practical examples, specialized conferences, field trips)
Computer lab practices (preparation and resolution of statistical and programming practical exercises)
Seminars (preparation and resolution of theoretical questions and practical problems in small groups, debates, collaborative problem-solving)
Non-contact learning activities (individual/autonomous study and group work for practice reports, problem-solving)
Tutorials (personalized support, individual or group, face-to-face or virtual)

assessment_methods.method: Set of activities proposed during the course (analysis and synthesis of topics, practical problems and exercises in groups, monographic works)
